a:r.a:t: Damage to Macromolecules Can Trigger Programmed Cell Death (Apoptosis)

p:cNvPr.descr: An image showing the process by which apoptosis occurs. An image of a yellow space, representing the cytoplasm of a cell, lined by the plasma membrane at the top. From top to bottom, a structure that comprises three fused wands is pointing into the cytoplasm. Each wand has three sections: a top gray knob, a light and dark red rolling pin-like structure in the middle, and a blue egg-like shape at the base. The gray part is labeled TNF alpha, the light red part of the rolling pin is labeled TNF alpha receptor, and the dark red and blue sections are labeled as death domains. Below that, a green oval, labeled procaspase-8, is seen at the right side of the cytoplasm. A curved arrow points from procaspase-8 to the left, indicating a darker green oval, labeled as caspase-8, with hair-like projections all around. From here, an arrow points down toward a gray structure with folds in the center, labeled as mitochondrion. Another arrow points down to cytochrome c, and the next arrow points down to apoptosome. Simultaneously, an incoming arrow indicated that apaf-1 is coming into the reaction before apoptosome. From here, a small line connected to a curved arrow shows a purple sphere, labeled as Procaspase-9, on the left and two darker purple spheres on the right with hair-like projections all around, labeled caspase-9. Three black arrows point down to text that reads, "Apoptosis." From Caspase 8, three successive curved arrows pointing down to the right show caspases 3,6,and 7. Another long arrow facing down and to the left points to apoptosis. A white arrow points away from apoptosis and into a a smaller yellow structure, similar to the cytoplasm and plasma membrane.
